open_obligations: Check whether expert iteration reaches anything close to an equilibrium of the protocols.
Note the authors list simplified training as a limitation.
Check the size of the improvement relative to the solo-verifier baseline and its variance across rollouts.
in.other_title: Code validation: all protocols modestly beat a solo verifier; nip and mnip gain about 11%
in.rationale: Anil et al. call for scaling PVGs to more challenging problems. Hammond and Adam-Day report that on APPS code validation every protocol modestly beats a verifier trained alone, with nip and mnip gaining about 11% and mnip best on worst-case performance; training is eight rounds of expert iteration rather than equilibrium-seeking methods.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether prover-verifier protocols help weak verifiers on a realistic task, for GPT-4o provers and GPT-4o-mini verifiers on APPS code validation

open_obligations: Check that grade-school math is 'more challenging' in the sense Anil et al. mean, given it has known answers.
Note that Kirchner et al. use a role-conditioned helpful/sneaky prover, not Anil et al.'s single prover that always argues for label 1.
Check how far from equilibrium the trained players are, since no equilibrium guarantee is given.
in.other_title: Prover-verifier games (checkability training) improve legibility of LLM math solutions
in.rationale: Anil et al. call for scaling PVGs to harder problems and studying behaviour at approximate equilibria. Kirchner et al. train GPT-4-family helpful and sneaky provers against much smaller verifiers on GSM and report rising helpful-prover accuracy, verifier robustness and human legibility; they train by coordinate descent toward an approximate local equilibrium and state the theory's prover-class assumption is not met.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether prover-verifier game training scales beyond toy tasks to LLMs trained toward approximate equilibria, on grade-school math

text: The authors call for scaling Prover-Verifier Games to more challenging problems, including ones with no known verification protocol, and state that since exact equilibria are hard to solve for, more work is needed to understand prover and verifier behaviour at approximate equilibria; they warn that deploying PVG-trained systems before an equilibrium is reached could lead to unexpected behaviour.
title: Open questions: scaling PVGs to harder problems and behaviour at approximate equilibria
